display_name: Israel's Interpretation Law 5741-1981 and Interpretation Ordinance [New Version], in L4 (Claude Sonnet 5.5 agents, working alone)
method: Claude Sonnet 5.5 agents working alone from written briefs: no ontology agent, no fleet, no integrator, and no independent test author in passes 1 and 2. Pass 1 (2026-10-13) encoded the time rules; pass 2 (2026-10-29) brought every unit of both texts to one disposition (226 units: encoded 123, fork 31, inert 15, repealed or blank 57). Expected values for the tests were decided from the statute text before the modules were run. A fix pass (2026-10-29) followed an independent test pass by another author (607 assertions on the pass-2 deposit: 590 satisfied, 13 failed, 4 refused, 37 gaps): it edited two pass-1 files (Law s. 26 and its tests), made open entries and lists answer by the rule in NOTES.md section 1, added the functions and tests for the gaps, and registered forks F35 to F38. The independent author's assertions are not in this folder.

encoded: Interpretation Law 5741-1981: every section and defined term. ss. 1 (gate, vintage), 2, 4 to 7, 9, 25 (rules of reading); 3 (all 26 entries and the opening words: day, year and month, fiscal year from pass 1, the other 23 in pass 2); 8, 10(a)(b)(c), 21 (time); 11 to 19 (scope of a grant of power); 20, 22(1) to (3), 23, 24, 26, 31, 32, 33
Interpretation Ordinance [New Version]: s. 1 (the 61 live entries, the earlier meanings that its notes state, and which enactments its definitions govern); ss. 16(4), 17, 19, 42

Rows with no L4 by design: ss. 27 to 30 of the Law and 53 units of the Ordinance read repealed or blank in the text; 15 units are not operative (titles, histories, headings, a signature, one editorial note)
explicit_not_covered: the Hebrew calendar (a period counted by it is a named refusal)
any calendar of holidays (days of rest, recess and holiday are an input)
periods counted backwards, 'within' periods and mixed units, which s. 10 does not speak of
the earlier meaning of 'enactment' (חיקוק) in an enactment given before the Ordinance: no text of the sources states it (named refusal)
the dates the provisos of Ordinance s. 1 turn on (the Ordinance's commencement, publication of its new text, the Movables Law and the Land Law): inputs
a day-level date on 1981-10-01 (named refusal; the moment-level function settles it)

scenarios the texts are silent on (deemed service, registered mail, hours, business days, a quorum for a majority act, schedules, a foreign State as a person, Hebrew-calendar arithmetic): no function, or a named refusal; the table in NOTES.md section 3 lists each

not_reviewed: Draft. No domain expert has read any of this against the statute, and no lawyer who knows Israeli law has seen the fork register (38 forks, none ruled). Both source texts are unofficial Hebrew Wikisource consolidations, and the encoding leans on Wikisource's editorial notes in several places; only s. 10 of the Law has been compared with an official PDF. The tests were written by the same agent that wrote the modules, with expected values decided from the statute text beforehand; there was no independent test author in passes 1 and 2. An independent test pass has run once, on the pass-2 deposit; its findings are fixed here, and this deposit has not been tested by an independent author again.
